 Log in Bednar returning to Yankees after accepting qualifying offer
 29 minutes ago Max Ralph
 Share share-square--:R1qlq: Closer David Bednar will return to the Yankees for 2027 after he accepted New York's one-year, $23.15 million qualifying offer on Tuesday.
 Bednar will now be under contract for 2027 and will be ineligible to receive another qualifying offer when he becomes a free agent next offseason. Players who received a qualifying offer had until Tuesday at 4 p.m. ET to decide if they would accept it. Bednar and Twins catcher Ryan Jeffers were the only players out of the eight who received the offer this offseason to accept.

• Qualifying offers: Bednar, Jeffers accept; 6 decline 
 Bednar was as good as ever in 2026, finishing the regular season with a 2.47 ERA and 35 saves in 39 opportunities. It was more evidence that the two-time All-Star has fully recaptured his peak form after uncharacteristic struggles in 2024.
 But the 32-year-old Bednar, who just completed his only full season in New York after being traded from the Pirates to New York in 2025, went about things a little differently this time.
 Relying on his hard four-seamer and a devastating curveball for much of his career, Bednar featured his splitter at an all-time high in 2026. He threw the offering 41.6% of the time, even surpassing the 40.6% share his fastball received. Relatedly, that was the least he used his four-seamer in any season of his career.
 It’s not hard to see why Bednar favored the split-finger pitch. It generated a 14 Run Value , the highest of any splitter in MLB this season. That included elite-level whiff (35.2%) and strikeout (32.7%) rates. Opponents slugged just .189 on Bednar’s splitter.
 Bednar’s fastball, by contrast, saw opponents hit .282 with a .423 slugging percentage. Bednar also averaged a career-low 96.1 mph on the four-seamer, a full tick down from the 97.1 mph he averaged in 2025. However, there may have been some bad luck mixed in. Opponents had an outsized .356 batting average on balls in play and just a .236 expected batting average on Bednar’s heater. And even his diminished velocity still ranked in the 77th percentile across MLB.
 The right-hander’s once-dominant curveball was hit hard in 2026 (two home runs, .536 SLG), but Bednar used it at the lowest rate of any full season in his career (18.2%).
 The 2027 season will be the ninth in the Majors for Bednar, a Pittsburgh-area native who was a 35th-round Draft pick of the Padres in 2016. He debuted with San Diego in 2019 and then was shipped to the Pirates in the January 2021 Joe Musgrove trade. “The Renegade” then became a dominant closer in his hometown, earning trips to the Midsummer Classic in 2022 and 2023. 
 Bednar then posted a 5.77 ERA in 2024, struggling with his command and allowing nine home runs in 62 outings. After a brief option to the Minor Leagues in April 2025, Bednar locked things back in with a 2.37 ERA before the Pirates dealt him to the Yankees, and he’s been excellent since.
